title: vpc-baseline: add NAT strategy options (single vs per-AZ) + installer outputs
author: Victor Alvarez
description: Context: For Private (VPC) alpha we need an opinionated default NAT posture, but also the ability to switch between a cost-optimized single NAT GW and a higher-availability per-AZ NAT GW pattern. The installer also needs stable outputs (subnet IDs + route table IDs + NAT info) so it can validate egress assumptions and render networking config. This PR adds a NAT strategy interface to modules/vpc-baseline, updates routes accordingly, and documents cost/availability tradeoffs. Changes: - Introduce `nat_mode` with allowed values: `none` | `single` | `per_az` (default: `single`). - Create NAT gateway(s) in public subnets when nat_mode != none. - Route private subnets to NAT gateway(s) based on nat_mode (single uses first public subnet NAT; per_az uses NAT in matching AZ). - Add input validations for common foot-guns (per_az requires >= 2 public subnets across distinct AZs; nat_mode=none disallows private subnets when `enable_private_egress_routes=true`, etc). - Add outputs consumed by redwood-private-installer: `nat_gateway_ids`, `nat_public_ips`, `private_route_table_ids`, and `public_subnet_ids_by_az`/`private_subnet_ids_by_az` (as maps). Notes on cost/ops: single NAT is materially cheaper (1x NAT GW hourly + fewer data processing charges) but is a single-AZ dependency; per-AZ improves AZ fault isolation at higher cost. We still recommend VPC endpoints for AWS services to reduce NAT data processing. Test plan: - `terraform fmt` - `terraform validate` - `examples/minimal` plan w/ nat_mode=single - `examples/minimal` plan w/ nat_mode=per_az (2 AZ) - Manual smoke: ensure private route tables point at NAT(s) and that outputs are stable (no diff on second plan). Checklist: - [x] Docs updated (README cost note + variable table) - [x] Added validation errors with actionable messages - [x] Outputs names reviewed with installer team (Benji/Ethan) - [x] Backwards compatibility notes (new defaults preserve existing behavior)

review_conversation: Irene Choi (review): Can we make the default explicit in the README and call out the cost delta? Also, per_az should fail fast if the public subnet list is 1 element or all in the same AZ. Victor Alvarez (author): Yep—added validation on `public_subnet_azs` distinct count and a short cost note with a link placeholder to the ops page (will be filled in day-2 doc). Nina Petrova (review): For per_az, are we ensuring the private subnet in us-west-2b routes to the NAT in us-west-2b (not just index alignment)? Victor Alvarez (author): Updated logic to build a map by AZ and route each private RT to the NAT in the same AZ; falls back to error if AZ mapping is incomplete. Benji Okafor (review): Installer needs stable outputs: route table IDs for private tiers + NAT public IP(s). Can we avoid output type changes across modes (string vs list)? Victor Alvarez (author): Outputs are always lists/maps; for nat_mode=none the list is empty. Added `private_route_table_ids` output and documented it for installer consumption. Sahana Iyer (review): CI flakes sometimes on NAT association ordering. Please add explicit dependencies to avoid eventual consistency issues with route creation. Victor Alvarez (author): Added `depends_on` from aws_route to nat gateway + igw attachments; re-ran workflow x2; both green. Irene Choi (final): Approved after validations + docs update.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; CHANGELOG entry added under Unreleased for vpc-baseline. Follow-up tracked in ENG-4827 to wire these outputs into redwood-private-installer networking config and preflight validations.
